slates.label: Thursday picks
slates.note: Week 11 Thursday: three parlays, every leg in a different game, built mostly on team markets (Panthers +9.5, Jaguars +2.5, Bills -3.5, Cowboys team total over 23.5) plus the three required locked-in props (Goff completions in a dome, Jonathan Taylor receiving tonight on TNF, McBride receiving). P(hit) 0.74 / 0.62 / 0.63 with EV +3.0%, -0.1% and +0.4%, staked $100 / $50 / $50 (no Tuesday/Thursday stake above $100).

parlays.why: Panthers +9.5 (-584): Carolina is the 3-pt home favorite (Pinnacle ML 58%) against a Ravens team on Jacoby Brissett with Lamar Jackson on IR and CB Marlon Humphrey sent home, so this loses only if Baltimore wins by 10+. Seven books price it and DK was still about 3 pts cheaper than the others' median; it shortened from -512 to -584 today while the rest of the market held. Fair 88.3% vs 86.6% no-vig (EPA model has CAR by about 6, shaded +1.6 pts), sunny 68F in Charlotte. Jared Goff 18+ completions (-529): he has cleared 17.5 in 8 of 9 games (mean 22.8, main line 21.5), plays every snap in the Ford Field dome, and has no injury designation. Tampa's Mayfield was limited Thursday and is at best 50/50. Fair 83.8% vs 84.4% market after the 1.5-pt prop haircut. Backtest leg cost about 3% + 8%; P 0.740 x 1.392 = 1.030, EV +3.0%, so $100.

Jaguars +2.5 (-361): Jacksonville is the 6-pt road favorite at the Giants and ranks 1st in my opponent-adjusted EPA ratings (model JAX by about 7.7). This loses only if the Giants win by 3+; fair 80.0% vs 77.5% no-vig (8 books; the +2.5-pt shade comes from the model). The forecast is light rain, which lowers variance. Jonathan Taylor 10+ receiving yards (-394) on TNF tonight in Houston's closed roof: 8 of 10 over 9.5 (15, 24, 18, 20 the last four, 3-5 targets a game), no injury tag. As a 12.5-pt underdog Indy should be throwing to its backs. DK moved from -269 Tuesday to -394 with the consensus following (0.77 to 0.82), so the market has moved our way, and Pinnacle's main is 19.5 at -134. Fair 78.0% vs 79.4% market after the haircut. Cost about 3% + 7%; P 0.624 x 1.601 = 0.999, EV -0.1%. It leans on the power shade (without it P x payout is 0.968), so $50.

Cowboys team total Over 23.5 (-550) indoors against a Titans defense allowing +0.09 EPA/play (4th worst); Dallas is implied for about 31 (total 54.5, DAL -8) after scoring 40 last week, and Ferguson being out is minor. Fair 84.9% vs 84.9% market, DK 2.9 pts cheaper than the other books. Bills -3.5 (-690) at home against a Dolphins team on Kyle McCord: Buffalo is a 16-pt favorite (93% ML), sunny 64F and 8 mph in Orchard Park; fair 87.5% vs 87.7%. Trey McBride 25+ receiving yards (-568): 10 of 10 over 24.5, the TE1 and target leader (Pinnacle main 49.5). Rookie Carson Beck's first completion went to him, and Arizona trails as a 15.5-pt underdog. Fair 84.9% vs 84.9% after the haircut. The new QB is the extra risk, so $50. Cost about 3% + 3% + 7%; P 0.631 x 1.591 = 1.004, EV +0.4%.

Steelers 68% vs 67% de-vigged: 4.5-pt road favorite at a 2-7 Eagles team without Hurts; my EPA model has PIT by about 6.

slates.label: Tuesday picks
slates.note: Week 11 Tuesday: three $50 parlays built mostly on team sides (Panthers +8.5, Titans +20.5, 49ers +6.5, Steelers +6.5) plus four locked-in-role props (Cousins completions, Chase Brown rush+rec yds, Chase rec yds), every leg in a different game. Week 10's line history showed short-priced prop Overs hitting 3-5 pts below the no-vig market, so props now carry a calibration haircut; that leaves every parlay just over the profit floor (EV about -2% to -3%), so all are minimum stakes.

parlays.why: Panthers +8.5 (-577) at home vs a Ravens team on Jacoby Brissett with Lamar Jackson on IR: CAR is the 2.5-pt favorite (Pinnacle ML 57%, line moved from CAR -1.5 toward Carolina), so this only loses if Baltimore wins by 9+; fair 85.5% vs 85.4% no-vig, 7 books, dry 70F in Charlotte. Kirk Cousins 18+ completions (-610): he has cleared 17.5 in 10 of 10 games this season (19-26 the last six), Kyler Murray (Grade 2 hamstring) is targeted for Week 12, and Minnesota is a 3-pt underdog in Mexico City so the volume should be there; fair 83.8% vs 83.8% market after a 1.5-pt prop calibration haircut. EV about -2% (P x payout 0.979), so $50.

Chase Brown 50+ rush+receiving yds (-497): Cincinnati's lead back has cleared 49.5 in 9 of 9 games (58-101, six straight at 58+) thanks to a steady receiving role (8 catches in two of his last three), no injury designation all season, and the Bengals are 6.5-pt favorites in a 52.5 total; fair 82.0% vs 82.0% market (4 books, DK's -497 beats the others' median). Titans +20.5 (-506) in Dallas's dome: only a Cowboys win by 21+ loses it; Dallas has allowed the most EPA/play in the league (584 yds to SF last week) and my power rating has this game at DAL by 2.6, not 8.9, but the line moved toward Dallas so I used only half that shade: fair 82.7% vs 81.6% market. EV -2.5% (P x payout 0.975), so $50. James Cook 70+ was the first choice here but slipped to 79.5% fair on the 19:05 re-poll and missed the floor.

Ja'Marr Chase 60+ rec yds (-463): 84-96% snaps the last four games, 11-14 targets in three straight, 7 of 9 over 59.5, and Washington is without Terry McLaurin, so Cincinnati (-6.5, moved from -3.5) should throw early and often; fair 80.7% vs 82.0% market after the haircut, dry 47F forecast for Monday. 49ers +6.5 (-451) at the neutral Mexico City site: SF is a 3-pt favorite (Pinnacle ML 60%), ranks 1st in my EPA power ratings, and only a Vikings win by 7+ loses it; fair 81.8% vs 81.2%. Steelers +6.5 (-620) at a 2-7 Eagles team with Jalen Hurts on IR and no named starter (Joe Milton started Week 9): PIT is the 4.5-pt favorite and loses this only by losing by 7+; fair 85.3% vs 85.8%, light-rain risk only. EV -2.9% (P x payout 0.971), so $50.

slates.label: Sunday picks
slates.note: Week 10 Sunday: five core parlays (joint 58-67%) built from low rungs on volume starters (most cleared their number in every 2026 game) plus consensus-anchored alt spreads where DK has the longest price, each core leg in a different game. I dropped a 6th core parlay because this morning's prices pushed it below the profit floor. Weather is benign everywhere. Thursday's WAS +11.5 hit. DK moneylines are again 1.5-5 pts worse than Pinnacle, so moneylines appear only in the bonus parlay.

parlays.why: Travis Kelce 25+ rec yds (fair 81.7% vs DK 80.0%): he cleared 24.5 in 6 of 7 games, the market mean is about 60 yds, and DK is 5 pts longer than the other books' median at this rung. Panthers +8.5 (fair 78.6% vs DK 77.8%; DK -350 is still at or longer than the other books, and New Orleans' Pinnacle win chance fell from 57% Thursday to 54%): New Orleans is only a 2.5-pt favorite in a dome, Pinnacle prices CAR +7.5 at -298 (DK -293), and +8.5 also covers losses by 7 and 8.

Hunter Henry 20+ rec yds (fair 79.4% vs DK 78.9%; the market line rose from 35.5 to 37.5 since Thursday): he cleared it in 6 of 7 games and the market mean is about 46; Munich is dry and 48°F. Trevor Lawrence 200+ pass yds (fair 78.4% vs DK 78.7%): the market mean is about 248, he reached 182+ in every game, and Nashville is sunny with 5 mph wind.

Javonte Williams 50+ rush+rec yds (fair 84.5% vs DK 84.8%): he has 50+ in all 7 games (19-25 carries lately), and the market mean is about 89; dome. Colts +3.5 (fair 78.7% vs DK 78.7%, Pinnacle prices the same rung at -394): Indianapolis is a 4-pt home favorite in a dome against a Miami offense with rookie QB McCord, so the Colts only need to avoid losing by 4+.

Matthew Stafford 150+ pass yds (fair 87.0% vs DK 87.0%): he has 157+ in every game and the market mean is about 213, in a dome. Ryan Flournoy 20+ rec yds (fair 77.6% vs DK 77.0%): he has 22+ in all 7 games, and Dallas is without TE Jake Ferguson and WR Jonathan Mingo, which frees up targets; dome.

Lions +8.5 (fair 84.1% vs DK 83.8%; Pinnacle has no market, and DK's -519 is the longest price across 7 books). Chase Brown 50+ rush+rec yds (fair 81.6%): 58+ in all 7 games, Cincinnati calm and 40°F. Panthers +11.5 (fair 84.1% vs DK 83.5%): New Orleans is only a 2.5-pt favorite. This one gets $50 because it shares the NO and DET games with other parlays and its EV is -0.3%.

Sunday 5-leg bonus: Stafford 150+ pass yds (86.9%; 157+ every game), Tyler Warren 20+ rec yds (87.6%), Javonte Williams 12+ rush attempts (85.4%; 19+ in his last 5), Panthers +11.5 (84.1%) and Lions +10.5 (87.3%), each in a different game. Groups: QB, WR/TE, RB, team. At most one leg is shorter than -700.

Sunday 5-leg bonus: Javonte Williams 50+ rush+rec yds (84.6%), Stafford 150+ pass yds (86.9%), McMillan 30+ rec yds (86.5%), Jonathan Taylor 40+ rush yds (83.7%) and Lions +10.5 (87.3%), each in a different game. It shares only Stafford and DET +10.5 with the other bonus parlay. Groups: RB, QB, WR/TE, team.

Sunday 5-leg moneyline bonus: Jaguars (my 84.8% vs Pinnacle 84.0%; Tennessee is missing WR Tate, G Skoronski and two starting LBs), Rams (82.6% vs 81.7%; Arizona is missing its C and a G), Bills (81% vs 80.6%), Seahawks (72% vs 71.9%; Drew Lock's start was announced Monday, so it is already in the line) and Chiefs (64% vs 63.4%; the line moved toward KC this morning even with RB Walker ruled out, and Atlanta is without WR Branch and LB Deablo). Since 2010, big favorites won about 1 pt more often than the closing line implied in both halves of the sample, and no other situational factor (divisional, rest, bye, road favorite) held up out of sample. I passed on Houston (66% by Pinnacle) because its defense is gutted (Hunter and Al-Shaair out, Anderson DNP), on SF because Evans is out and Trent Williams didn't practice, and on Baltimore and Indianapolis because both are under 67% and their DK prices are 2.5-4 pts worse than Pinnacle's.

slates.label: Thursday picks
slates.note: Week 10 Thursday: three short parlays (joint 74%, 71%, 64%), every leg in a different game, built from low rungs on volume starters plus Washington +11.5 tonight in the rain. Nothing new was graded yet (the Tuesday slate's games start tonight). This run fixed an alt-line bug that faked 3-4% edges at +2.5 spreads, and the lowest receiving rungs are now priced with a dud-game allowance.

parlays.why: James Cook 60+ rush yds (-500): Buffalo is an 8.5-pt favorite at the Jets in a sunny, 49F MetLife game; Cook has 21-31 carries in his last four games and cleared 59.5 in 7 of 8 (median 101); fair 85.7% vs 83.5% book (Pinnacle-anchored market 83.3%; other books' median price at this rung implies 86.4%). CeeDee Lamb 50+ rec yds (-552) in the Dallas dome: 11-21 targets in each of his last five full games, 7 of 9 over 49.5 (the misses were a 57%-snap injury game and Week 1); TE Jake Ferguson is out, George Pickens is questionable, and SF's secondary has two CBs who were DNP; fair 86.6% vs 85.1% book. Different games, both with Pinnacle mains, so it gets the top stake.

Commanders +11.5 tonight (-470): the Giants are only 1.5-pt favorites (Pinnacle ML 54%) and the line moved toward Washington since Tuesday; only a Giants win by 12+ loses it. Light rain (74%) should keep scoring down, which helps a big alt spread. DK's price is the best on the board (other books -525 to -625); fair 84.5% vs 82.5% book. Geno Smith 170+ pass yds (-459) at home vs Buffalo: the Jets will likely trail by 8.5, he has 30+ attempts in 7 of his last 8 starts and 7 of 9 games over 169.5, and Sunday's MetLife forecast is dry; fair 83.4% vs 82.1% book. Staked $50 because Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable and the TNF fair comes from interpolating Pinnacle's ladder.

Jahmyr Gibbs 16+ rush attempts (-462) in Munich (dry, about 38F): 15-29 carries every game, 7 of 8 over 15.5, and Detroit's backups Vaki (DNP) and Saylors (out) are hurt; fair 84.3% vs 82.2% book. Chris Olave 40+ rec yds (-576) in the Saints' dome: 6-13 targets and 43+ yds in all 8 games (rookie Jordyn Tyson's snaps are rising, so fair is held near market); fair 85.6% vs 85.5% book. Travis Kelce 20+ rec yds (-680) in Atlanta's dome: 7 of 8 over 19.5, and he and Mahomes (elbow) were both full participants Wednesday; fair 88.8% vs 87.2% book. Three games and three position groups, about +5% EV.

slates.label: Sunday picks
slates.note: Week 9 Sunday: six short, high-hit-rate parlays (joint 66-77%) built from 14 low-rung legs across 12 different games: QBs, RBs, WRs, tackles, kickers and two team totals. Thursday's JAX ML + Starks parlay won. Lessons applied: no unders or TD/sack props, no QB-change offenses, no legs reused from Tue/Thu, and every leg cleared its rung in nearly every 2026 game. It's a dry week, so weather removed no legs.

parlays.why: Josh Allen has thrown for 170+ in all 7 starts (253/210/255/289 lately) and plays indoors against a Wentz-led MIN team (fair 88% vs book 89% at -840); Ka'imi Fairbairn has made 1+ FG in 7 of 7 games, and HOU@LAC is indoors with a 40.5 total that points to field goals (fair 87% vs book 89% at -810). Every leg is from a different game, so the legs are independent: joint 76% (still 73% under conservative de-vig), paying 1.26x.

Mahomes has 190+ pass+rush yards in 6 of 7 games, at home against a NYJ secondary missing CB Nahshon Wright (fair 87% vs book 89% at -800); HOU CB Kamari Lassiter plays every snap and has 2+ solo tackles in 6 of 7 games (7/3/6/5 lately) against pass-first LAC (fair 89% vs book 90% at -900). Every leg is from a different game, so the legs are independent: joint 77% (still 73% under conservative de-vig), paying 1.25x.
